title: Tiered request prioritization + elastic connection pool for downstream resilience
creator: Ava Chen
description: Add a tiered request prioritization layer and an elastic connection pool that can shrink/grow per-tenant and per-region, combined with soft circuit-breakers and progressive load-shedding policies to improve downstream dependency resilience (Redis/Kafka/Primary DB). Goal: keep tail latency within SLOs during partial outages and maintain graceful degradation for best-effort requests.
acceptance_criteria: New elastic connection pool implementation deployed behind feature flag in staging
Tiered priority queues (P0/P1/P2) applied at front-door with documented admission rules
Circuit-breaker opens for a dependency when error-rate > configured threshold for 30s and closes via rolling probe policy
Automated load-shedding path for P2 requests with 95th-percentile drop < 10% under a simulated 30% downstream capacity loss
Latency and error dashboards for per-tenant, per-region SLOs populated and reviewed
Canary rollout plan and rollback playbook validated in staging and dry-run executed in prod window
notes: Background: recent incident 2026-02-24 showed pan-regional Redis latency spike cascading to request timeouts and a full connpool stall under head-of-line blocking. Existing connpool is static per-process and does not differentiate request importance.

Design goals: avoid head-of-line blocking, preserve high-priority (P0) user-facing requests, provide predictable degradation for background jobs and non-critical calls, and minimize amplification risk (thundering herd) on failover.

High-level approach: implement request tagging at the API gateway -> assign priority score -> admission controller consults local elastic connpool and per-dependency health state -> use token-bucket based admission per-priority lane -> evict/queue/redirect lower priority requests when pools are saturated.

Connpool behavior: use a hybrid strategy combining a bounded per-tenant min pool and an elastic soft-max that allows temporary bursts controlled by a global shared semaphore. Pools shrink after an idle timeout and release file descriptors to the OS to avoid resource pressure.

Circuit-breaker policy: multi-stage - fast conservative open based on error-rate and d’slo breach, with a background probing scheduler that ramps probes exponentially and only routes a small fraction of P1/P2 traffic when half-open.

Load-shedding policy: deterministic drop for P2 requests when admission queue > configured watermark. For P1 we employ probabilistic shedding tied to observed downstream latency percentiles to reduce variance in tail latency.

Trade-offs: adding per-request priority and admission increases code paths and potential for misclassification; we mitigate with strict default mappings and observability. Elastic pools reduce cold-start latency vs rigid pools but add complexity in sizing heuristics.
Security&Compliance: no sensitive data changes. KMS/HSM unaffected. Security review not required for initial MVP but will be requested if any auth path is modified.
Operational concerns: need clear SLOs and runbooks for when circuit-breaker misfires; add automated rollback triggers based on error budget burn rate and 1-min error-rate spike detection.

implementation_steps: 1) Add request priority propagation to API ingress and ensure SDKs set correct hints for internal calls
2) Implement elastic connpool library with per-tenant min and soft-max, global shared semaphore, and shrink strategy
3) Integrate lightweight circuit-breaker state machine per dependency with metrics and probe scheduler
4) Implement admission controller with token-bucket per-priority lane and deterministic shedding logic
5) Add observability: per-priority qps, accept/drop counts, pool size, wait times, probe success/failures, and per-tenant SLO dashboards
6) Run staged chaos tests in staging (service-disruption, partial Redis/Kafka/Disk IO degradation), tune thresholds
7) Gradual canary rollout to <5% of production traffic with automatic rollback if burn-rate > threshold
8) Full rollout with runbook and post-deploy monitoring window
observability_requirements: metric: connpool.active_size and connpool.wait_time percentile per-service
dashboard: per-tenant SLO heatmap (latency, errors) with 1m and 5m resolution
alert: error_budget_burn_rate > 2x over 5m triggers rollback to previous rollout version
testing_plan: Unit tests for pool sizing, semaphore behavior, and token-bucket admission
Integration tests against Redis emulator and Kafka stub to validate queueing and shedding behavior
Staging chaos tests: simulate 30-60% node loss, network partition, elevated packet loss to validate circuit-breaker and probe behavior
Load test: sustained QPS at 1.5x normal with injected 50ms latency on Redis to observe tail behavior
Canary in prod: start with internal tenants, then selected external tenants with low blast radius
